pairs.subject: breach-alerting-and-attribution
pairs.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_observability/libs/useGlobalAlertEvaluator.ts:53 evaluates every rule against an UNSCOPED 1-day bundle (and useObservabilityData.ts:70 against the tab's range/persona) under the one rule.id cooldown the scoped Rust evaluator also reads, so a client fire on the wrong window or scope mutes the correct server alert for an hour

techniques.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_observability/libs/useGlobalAlertEvaluator.ts:53 getOverviewBundle(1) passes no persona, so a persona-scoped rule is judged on global metrics, and the client persists that fire to fired_alerts, where the Rust loop's rule.id cooldown reads it. The detection path is outside the key, which is right, but the three paths compute different conditions

src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:153 the toast and history message is only '<metric> is <value> (threshold ...)'. A cost breach names no persona or model contributor, even though per-persona cost rollups already exist (homework alert)
src/features/overview/sub_observability/libs/useGlobalAlertEvaluator.ts:25 evaluation runs on a 60s timer, not in an admission decision; there is no ingest path for delivery to tax
src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:153 rules scope only by persona (operator's own agents), never by API key or customer; no identity axis exists to refuse

pairs.registryProposal: The scope-carrying evaluator src-tauri/src/commands/execution/alert_evaluator.rs (tick at :191, which publishes alert_fired at :300 to the Slack/Discord webhook notifier) belongs to NO context in context-map.json, so no pair can judge the server half of this subject. Also: the golden path's audience precondition should mention the hybrid case seen here (a local instrument whose payload is ALSO forwarded to an operator-configured broadcast webhook).

pairs.subject: breach-alerting-and-attribution
pairs.evidence: src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:450 evaluateRule runs a persona-scoped rule against whatever snapshot the caller passed and ignores rule.persona_id, then :431 shares one rule.id cooldown with the scoped server evaluator, so a wrong-scope client fire both misreports the value and suppresses the true alert

techniques.evidence: src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:431 the cooldown key is rule.id, while the condition behind it is computed over 1 day, over the tab range, or per persona, depending on the caller. The cost_spike baseline at :407 averages the caller's chart window, so on the 1-day global path it degenerates to roughly 1x
src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:153 formatAlertMessage carries no contributor list, share or figure; FiredAlert has no attribution field
src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:497 the evaluator writes the UI first and then persists best-effort through api.createFiredAlert, with pending-sync retry and no blocking on the sink
